title: I'm not a programmer, but I shipped an iOS arcade shooter with AI writing the code. Here's me on 1 heart vs. the wave 12 boss
author: highlandapps-team
selftext:
I run a sales team by day and have zero coding background. Strikeverse is a vertical arcade space shooter that's now live on the App Store. AI wrote basically all of the code; I handled the game design, the testing, and a LOT of playing.  
How it actually worked:  
I described what I wanted in plain English (enemy waves, boss phases, power-ups, the Lucky Wheel), the AI wrote it, and I played every build on my phone and reported what felt wrong.  
Boss fights took the most back-and-forth. Getting attack patterns that feel hard but fair took many rounds of "too easy / now impossible."  
The hardest part wasn't the code. It was App Store submission, in-app purchases, and all the account setup.  
What I learned: AI can write the game, but it can't tell you whether it's fun. That part still comes down to playing it over and over.  
Happy to answer questions about the workflow. Curious how others here handle balancing difficulty with AI help.
